_meta.title: LUNAPOLE physical constants — VERIFIED
_meta.rule: Anything not in this file is unverified. Do not hardcode a number that isn't here.

lunar._radius_note: spec used 1737400 for both. Real flattening is ~0.0012. Negligible for our tolerance; noted for honesty.

solar._verified: Max sun elevation at pole = lunar obliquity. Sun diameter 0.5334 (range 0.5246-0.5425).

derived.shadow_formula: L = h / tan(elevation_deg); at 1.5424 deg -> L = 37.20 * h
derived.curvature_formula: h_sphere = R * (1 - cos(theta / R))  [theta in metres]

CORRECTED_curvature_table._warning: The original spec's curvature numbers were WRONG by ~6x. These are verified values. The original claimed 42.2m at 30km and 469m at 100km.

values._note: the original spec's '42.2 m at 30 km' is actually the 12.1 km value

CORRECTED_curvature_table._impact: Far-field curvature correction is ~6x stronger than the spec assumed. Ridge shadows reach much further than believed. This STRENGTHENS the case that far-field is mandatory, but all horizon numbers must be recomputed.

earth_elevation_verified._note: Verified by direct computation of cos(theta)=sin(p)s sin(p)e + cos(p)s cos(p)e cos(dlon); elev = 90 - theta

mazarico_2011.status: CORRECT — the spec's hedge can be removed
mazarico_2011.authors: Mazarico, E., Neumann, G.A., Smith, D.E., Zuber, M.T., Torrence, M.H.
mazarico_2011.title: Illumination Conditions of the Lunar Polar Regions Using LOLA Topography
mazarico_2011._what_it_actually_does: Precomputes horizon elevation per azimuthal direction at 0.5 deg resolution from 240 m/px DEMs. For each surface point compares sun elevation to horizon profile per direction. If sun elevation < horizon elevation in ALL directions the point is in permanent shadow. THIS IS EXACTLY the max-per-azimuthal-bin method the spec proposes.
mazarico_2011._bonus_fact: Found Shackleton crater rim has ~240 days/year of continuous sunlight. Useful cross-check target.

astronomy-engine.status: DOES NOT WORK FOR THIS PROJECT
astronomy-engine.reason: No lunar-surface observer API. Observer/VectorObserver functions are Earth-surface only. Cannot compute Sun/Earth elevation from a point on the Moon.
astronomy-engine.usable_for: general astronomy display only, NOT for our observer

de440s_bsp._note: Use this, NOT de440.bsp (114 MB). Same Moon/Sun/Earth accuracy for our horizon work. Saves 82 MB.

moon_pa_bpc._note: CORRECTION: spec claimed ~1 MB. Actual 12.3 MB. Lunar orientation + libration kernel.

ldem_75s._note: Spec assumed a single ~1 GB file at 118 m/px. LOLA gridded products are distributed as TILES via PDS/Astrogeology, not one file. LDEM_87S as described in the spec DOES NOT EXIST as a standard product. PERSON 1 MUST resolve the exact tile URLs before any build starts. This is the single biggest schedule risk.
ldem_75s._spec_error: 25 m/px is NOT achievable from LOLA alone. That would need LROC NAC stereo DEMs (~1-2 m/px) which have limited, non-contiguous coverage. Decide: 118 m/px LOLA (honest, limited) or LROC NAC where available (better, patchy).

gazetteer_api.status: NO WORKING REST ENDPOINT — verified 404/HTML on multiple paths
gazetteer_api._note: Coordinates in sites.json came from Wikipedia infoboxes that cite IAU feature IDs. Always re-confirm at planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov by hand before publishing.
